requirements: docs/52 Security gates: fuzzers for the protocol decoder, path normalizer, tool argument validation and event migration; property tests for the effect receipt chain and lease fencing
docs/52 Major threats and controls: path traversal/symlink escape (incl. TOCTOU), shell injection
docs/55 prove the test detects broken behaviour (mutation beside each property)
scenarios: arbitrary bytes never panic the frame reader; a declared length above the ceiling is refused before it is read; written frames read back identical; a corrupted prefix never yields a frame

hostile paths are refused or resolve inside the root; planted links to the outside are refused; protected names are refused under any prefix; a target swapped for an escaping link between two operations is refused at the second
every registered tool's schema accepts or refuses arbitrary JSON without panicking, refuses undeclared keys and holds its string bounds
arbitrary receipt chains verify; every single-field tamper, reorder and interior deletion is detected; a verifier with one check removed accepts what the real one refuses
on the real SQLite store only the current lease generation lands; migrations are idempotent across reopen; rebuilt projections match
hostile metacharacter arguments reach the child as single literal tokens through the real broker; nothing named inside them runs

ci.note: all 14 checks green on macOS, Linux and Windows; the first run (35820462397) failed on Windows only because the TOCTOU test's Unix-only imports were unused there under -D warnings, fixed in a0f80fa

audit: IMPLEMENTED-PARTIAL before: every docs/52 threat had hand-written qualifications, but no randomized suite existed, no TOCTOU race was tested and no hostile-metacharacter argument had gone through the real broker.
proof: Randomized property suites over the real components (protocol reader, PathPolicy/WorkspaceService, the tool registry, the receipt-chain verifier, the SQLite event store, the terminal broker) run by cargo test --workspace on every platform; the path fuzzer found a real defect (a backslash on Unix named a literal file while the record rewrote it to '/'), fixed in crates/workspace/src/paths.rs.
negative_proof: Mutations inside the suites: a verifier without the hash check accepts a field tamper and one without the link check accepts a reorder; a corrupted length prefix never yields a frame; a stale lease generation writes nothing. The fuzzer's finding is the negative proof of the previous normalizer.
limitations: Property suites, not coverage-guided fuzzing (cargo-fuzz needs a nightly toolchain the pinned build does not use); bounded case counts; SAST/dependency/secret scanning, the signed SBOM and the external penetration test are M10.2 and the release procedure; the M8 sandbox/SSRF and cross-tenant matrices are not re-randomized.
